\section*{Test sheet: the axis of a mirror-symmetric mark}
The mark-axis rule (stage 4) puts a symmetric mark's anchor $X$ on its axis, and takes the axis to be the centre of the mark's ink bounds, with the slant removed.
The open decision in the report (``Mark anchor model'', ``Open decisions'') suggested that a more precise axis would be the line about which the outline best matches its mirror image,
or, for the tilde, zigzag and vertical tilde, the centre about which it best matches its rotation by 180°, since their terminals could push the bounds off centre.

This sheet measures that axis for every mark in \verb|SYMMETRIC_ABOVE| (except the combining letters, which are not mirror-symmetric and have their own measures in \verb|AXIS_MEASURE|) and \verb|SYMMETRIC_BELOW|,
and the symmetric \verb|.cap| forms, in the four patched fonts.
Method: the outline, de-slanted at the style's declared slant, is scanned into ink intervals every half unit of height;
the mirror axis is the $x$ that maximizes the overlap of the outline with its mirror image (searched to $\pm30$ units of the bbox centre, refined to 0.025);
the rotation centre is the point that maximizes the overlap with the outline rotated by 180°. For each mark the symmetry with the smaller mismatch is used.
$\Delta$ is the symmetry axis minus the bbox centre: how far the anchor would move.

\subsection*{Result}
Across all 204 glyphs, the largest $|\Delta|$ is 2.2 units (semibold italic \verb|breve.cap|); 188 of 204 are under 1 unit.
The tilde-like marks (tilde, tilde below, perispomeni, vertical tilde, zigzag, almost equal to, not tilde, homothetic) match their 180° rotation about a centre within 1.3 units of the bbox centre;
their mirror axis is meaningless (the search hits its $\pm30$ limit, mismatch about 50\%).
Not tilde (U+034A) and homothetic (U+034B) match neither symmetry exactly (mismatch about 10\%), since they combine a tilde with straight strokes, but the rotation centre is still within 1 unit.
The italic and semibold italic dots (U+0307, U+0308) are skewed ovals: their mirror mismatch is 13\%, their rotation mismatch small, and both axes are on the bbox centre.

\textbf{Decision to make:} none of the differences reaches 5 units; the biggest is 2.2, and the anchors are integers.
Recommendation: keep the bbox centre, and move the item from ``Open decisions'' to ``Decided: left as they are'' with these figures.
